outcome: No blocking finding in the focused writer change. This is bounded source review and inert/synthetic-file validation, not formal security approval, live settlement or durable custody qualification.
sourceAssessment: Exclusive O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW acquisition refuses existing final leaves, including symlinks and FIFO, without opening them for writing. Initial mode is 0600; fchmod, all writes, fsync and close address the same acquired descriptor.

Exact bytes input is required before acquisition. Strict positive integer progress advances only the unwritten suffix; invalid progress and application-visible write exceptions refuse without retry. Complete acceptance precedes one file fsync and one close attempt.

A writer-body BaseException survives secondary close failure by identity. Close-only failure propagates, and an unsuccessful open has no guessed close. The enclosing retention method preserves its existing current-attempt precedence and sticky private first-failure reference while draining only ownership already eligible for disposal.

Existing retention state, sampler identity/inactivity gate, disposal order, public payload schema and numeric limits are unchanged. Only the artifact writer call replaces write_text plus pathname chmod.

SparseDiagnostics standard pickle refusal uses from None, suppressing active exception context for ordinary rendering while retaining trusted private inspection. It does not prevent all in-process access or sanitize the existing sampler error-string payload.

Updated rollback tests inject the new writer boundary and correctly expect permissions before bytes. Actual writer integration and existing owner gates are separately exercised, including cleanup failure and second-retention refusal.

coverage.source: Entire new writer and serialization method, exact retention integration and test diff, complete new test module, handoff document; baseline function and control comparisons. Adjacent suites are the authorized injected/AST selections, not a whole-stack audit.
coverage.filesystem: Three test-created TemporaryDirectory cases only: preexisting regular/symlink/dangling/FIFO/directory refusal, exact private-mode bytes, synthetic pathname replacement demonstrating descriptor identity without name custody.

limitations: Trusted ancestors/root and synchronous single-owner assumptions remain. No directory FD, anchored resolver, directory fsync, atomic publication, authenticated evidence transport or durable recovery owner is implemented.

Partial, empty or possibly complete artifacts can remain after refusal; no unlink, overwrite or numeric-descriptor retry occurs. Ambiguous close may leave an unaccounted resource. A replaced pathname can point elsewhere even while the writer correctly uses its original inode.

Payload length bounds loop progress only. Aggregate serialized allocation, existing unbounded diagnostic strings, memory, blocking I/O latency and recovery capacity remain unqualified. No production budget or new quota is invented.
No hostile-process filesystem race, real sampler/process settlement, crash/power-loss persistence or loaded-image claim follows from these tests.
No image rebuild or artifact-byte revalidation was performed. Prior run.py, launch guards and specimen bytes were compared against baseline; no live use or authorization was added.
